plan.design: Round 1: measure the 12 highest-ESM-2 variants (spanning positions 2,12,14,19,22,23,24,37,39,40,43). Compute Spearman correlation between E1 (ESM-2) and E3 (measured fitness). Round 2: use round-1 results to score (ESM-2) and measure additional substitutions at positions showing high measured fitness, plus next-tier ESM-2 candidates. Final: rank 5 by highest E3.
controls: Same WT sequence and single-substitution constraint
all candidates scored by the same masked-marginal ESM-2
measurement via the same historical DMS oracle. Negative/low-ESM-2 candidates serve as implicit controls.
plan.observation_metric: Spearman rho(E1,E3) on round-1 sample; number of round-1 measured candidates at/above the 75th percentile of measured fitness; agreement of top-5 E1 with top-5 E3.
plan.refutation_condition: rho <= 0, OR fewer than 2 of the top-5 ESM-2 candidates are in the measured top quartile, OR the top ESM-2 candidate measures in the bottom half.

revision: H2: High measured fitness clusters at positions with demonstrated tolerance in round 1 (position 12 especially); the best 5 mutants are found by measuring chemically diverse substitutions at tolerant positions, not by ESM-2 rank alone. Falsifier: if no new candidate at these positions measures above +0.13, position tolerance does not generalize.
reason: Round-1 data refutes the assumption that ESM-2 top-rank directly yields top measured fitness (rho=0.126; top-ESM-2 S37N measured only +0.137 while rank-9 S12A measured +0.467). ESM-2 is only a weak prior; measured fitness is the authoritative signal.
